discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of time-reversal-invariant topological insulators
subfield: Condensed matter physics: topological phases of matter
motivation: Kane and Mele (2005) showed that spin-orbit coupling can produce a new insulating phase that preserves time-reversal symmetry, the quantum spin Hall state. They identified the Z2 topological invariant that separates it from ordinary band insulators and guarantees protected helical edge states. With others, Kane extended the idea to three-dimensional topological insulators with Dirac surface states. In 2007 Molenkamp's group observed quantized edge conductance in HgTe quantum wells, the first experimental realization of this phase, after a proposal by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang. The work established that symmetry and topology classify phases of matter even without interactions. That insight reorganized condensed matter physics. It led to the periodic table of topological phases, Weyl semimetals, topological superconductors and the search for Majorana modes, and it now guides the study of strongly correlated topological states. Few conceptual advances of the past two decades match it in depth, universality and experimental confirmation.
